body:
_Migrated from issue #962, filed 2026-07-17._

Found by the v4.1.15 adversarial pre-tag gate (auth/SPA lens), not by a user report. Filing so it is tracked rather than lost.

## Symptom

Save a default library view, then click **Edit default view** in the notice on the library page. The Advanced search form opens empty. The saved filter is never loaded, so "editing" it means retyping it from scratch.

## Why

#928 rewrote `Library` to render `<Catalog defaultFilter={…} />` (`frontend/src/App.tsx:51`). Before that, `Library` rendered `<AdvancedSearch defaultFilter={…} />` when a default filter existed, which is how the saved filter used to reach the form — on the wrong page, which was the bug #928 fixed.

The `/search` route renders `<AdvancedSearch />` with no props (`frontend/src/App.tsx:200`), so `AdvancedSearch`'s `defaultFilter` prop (`AdvancedSearch.tsx:52,58,60`) is now dead code. TypeScript can't flag an unused optional prop, so nothing caught it.

Net effect: users who had a saved default filter could previously see it in the form; now no surface pre-fills it. They can still **Clear default**, or overwrite it by submitting a new search, but they cannot inspect or edit it.

## The fix is not "pass the prop"

Passing `me.catalog?.default_filter` to the `/search` route unconditionally would pre-fill the form for **every** Advanced search visit, so someone opening Advanced search from the nav to run an ordinary search would silently get their default filter applied. That trades this bug for a worse one.

The link needs to signal intent — e.g. `/search?default=1` (`Catalog.tsx:522` currently links to plain `/search`), with `AdvancedSearch` pre-filling only when that is present. Worth confirming the query-param shape against how the rest of the SPA handles search state before implementing.

## Test coverage gap

`e2e/default-library-view.spec.ts:145` only asserts `advanced-search-form` has count 0 — i.e. that the library isn't the search page. Nothing clicks the edit link or asserts pre-fill, which is why a half-applied fix passed. A fix here should add that assertion.

Related: #928 also added `default-library-view.spec.ts` to the **mobile** project's `testIgnore` (`playwright.config.ts:65-70`) for documented shared-seed-login account-state races. The reason is legitimate and the spec still runs on desktop, but the mobile cell of this feature's viewport axis is manual-only rather than CI-enforced.

Ships as-is in v4.1.15: #928's headline fix (the library keeps its chrome, the notice, and "Show all books") works, and this is a secondary affordance.
title: "Edit default view" opens a blank Advanced search form
